Why it matters
Your brand core is a one-page summary of who you are. Everything you write and post comes from it. Brands without one often end up competing on price and discounts. Brands with one need fewer discounts, because trust does the selling.

Step by step
1. Describe 2 or 3 types of customer. Note their goals, what bugs them and where they spend time online.
   What good looks like: You have 2 or 3 short customer descriptions.
2. Write your brand promise in one sentence (why choose us).
   What good looks like: You have one promise sentence.
3. Pick three words for your personality and three words you never use.
   What good looks like: You have a six-word voice guide.
4. Write two or three values, each with one thing you actually do that proves it.
   What good looks like: Every value has proof, not just a claim.
5. Write your story in under 100 words: why the brand exists. Then save all five answers on one page.
   What good looks like: A one-page brand core is saved where your team, freelancers and AI tools can read it.

Key takeaway
Brands with one need fewer discounts, because trust does the selling.

Day 7 of 72 · Attract · The creative management cycle

Why it matters
Making ads works best as a loop you repeat every week or two. Each turn of the loop makes the next batch smarter, because winners teach you why they won.

Step by step
1. Research: spend 20 minutes reading reviews and comments. Browse rivals' ads in the Meta Ad Library (facebook.com/ads/library) and note trends.
   What good looks like: You have 3 to 5 notes on what buyers say and what others run.
2. Plan: pick the pillar (topic), the angle (reason to buy) and the one thing you will test.
   What good looks like: You have a one-line test, for example "Prove pillar, durability angle, testing review-led hook vs demo hook".
3. Brief: write one page per concept (ad idea) using the template in Lesson 7.9.
   What good looks like: Each concept has a brief anyone can produce from.
4. Produce: make the ads yourself, with creators or with AI editing tools.
   What good looks like: You have finished files in 4:5 and 9:16 sizes.
5. Launch: put the new ads live as a batch, not one at a time.
   What good looks like: All new ads start on the same day so they are judged fairly.
6. Learn: after 7 days, score each ad and write one line on why each winner won.
   What good looks like: Your next brief starts from written learnings, not guesses.

Key takeaway
Each turn of the loop makes the next batch smarter, because winners teach you why they won.

Day 11 of 72 · Attract · Testing campaigns vs scaling campaigns

Why it matters
Keeping testing and winning separate stops new tests from upsetting what already works. Three kinds of campaign do the job: scaling, testing and build.

Step by step
1. Create a build campaign that is always switched off, and build each new ad there once.
   What good looks like: You have a paused campaign holding every ad you have made.
2. Make a testing campaign (or test ad set) with 20 to 30% of the budget. Put each new batch of ads there.
   What good looks like: New ads get a fixed, fair budget away from your winners.
3. Keep proven ads in scaling campaigns with 70 to 80% of the budget. Do not add new ads to them while they are winning.
   What good looks like: Scaling campaigns stay stable.
4. When a test ad wins, copy it into a scaling campaign with Use existing post. That way it keeps its post ID, likes and comments.
   What good looks like: The winner runs in scaling with its social proof intact.

Key takeaway
Three kinds of campaign do the job: scaling, testing and build.

Ten minutes of setup before you spend money stops the most costly Meta problems. These are lost sales tracking, hacked accounts and spending that runs away. Do it once, one step at a time, and check it again every quarter.

Step by step
1. Go to business.facebook.com/settings and click Users > People, then Invite people. Invite a second person you trust with Full control (Meta's name for admin).
   What good looks like: People lists two people with full control.
2. In the same Business Settings, open Security Centre. Switch on Two-factor authentication for everyone: a code from your phone as well as a password.
   What good looks like: Security Centre shows two-factor required for all admins.
3. Still in Security Centre, click Start verification. Enter your legal business name, address, phone and website, exactly as on your official records (see Meta: verify your business).
   What good looks like: Verification shows "In review" or "Verified". If you see "Ineligible for verification" or no button, you do not need it yet. Skip it and come back later.
4. Add the Facebook & Instagram sales channel in Shopify.
   What good looks like: Facebook & Instagram appears under Sales channels, with your business, ad account, Page and pixel connected. See Shopify: set up Facebook & Instagram.
5. Turn data sharing up to Maximum.
   What good looks like: Data sharing reads "Maximum".
6. Open Events Manager (All tools > Events Manager) and click your pixel. Look at the Purchase row in the Overview tab.
   What good looks like: Purchase shows events from both Browser and Server, in your store's currency. If it shows nothing, place a small test order and check again in an hour.

Day 15 of 72 · Attract · Setting up target audiences

Why it matters
Audiences tell each platform who already knows you. Then cold campaigns find new people and warm campaigns reach the right ones. Set them up once on Meta, Google and TikTok, then reuse them in every campaign.

Step by step
1. On Meta, set audience groups for the whole account in Advertising settings > Audience segments (under All tools). Add your engaged audience (visitors and social engagers) and existing customers (customer list or store link).
   What good looks like: Reports show how much spend reaches brand-new people.
2. On Meta, click Audiences, then Create audience, then Custom audience, once for each.
   What good looks like: Every custom audience shows "Ready".
3. On Meta, build lookalikes of buyers or best customers. Make them at 1%, 3 to 5% and 10% for later tests.
   What good looks like: Three lookalike sizes are ready.
4. Set cold targeting to broad: your country and age 18 to 65+. Pick all genders unless the product is clearly for one. Choose who to leave out of cold ads: nobody, recent buyers, or all buyers and engagers. Meta announced in 2025 it is retiring its old past-customer spend cap, so check Ads Manager for your account. To keep past buyers out of cold ads, exclude your customer audiences. Then watch the Audience segments breakdown.
   What good looks like: Cold campaigns reach new people on purpose.
5. On Google, give it signals and words to avoid.
   What good looks like: Google has signals to guide it and words to avoid.
6. On TikTok, copy the same layers.
   What good looks like: TikTok has the same audience layers as Meta.

Key takeaway

Why it matters
GST (goods and services tax) is 10% on most local sales once you are registered. The money you collect is held for the ATO (the tax office), not earned by you, so set it aside.

1. Check your GST turnover (this month plus the last 11). Register within 21 days of reaching $75,000. Or register as soon as you expect to reach it within 12 months (see ATO: GST).
   What good looks like: You know whether you must register.
2. Once registered, show prices to local customers with GST included and issue tax invoices.
   What good looks like: Checkout prices include GST.
3. Open a separate bank account and each week move one eleventh of GST-inclusive sales into it.
   What good looks like: The GST bill is already saved when it is due.
4. Send in your BAS (business activity statement) on time. Quarterly due dates are 28 October, 28 February, 28 April and 28 July (see ATO: BAS due dates).
   What good looks like: Dates are on your calendar. Lodging online may add two weeks, except for the December quarter.
5. Claim GST credits on business costs that include GST, like local stock and services. Keep the tax invoices.
   What good looks like: Your BAS includes your credits.
6. In Helix Settings, keep My prices include GST/VAT on Use my country's default (or Yes if the sales you type include GST).
   What good looks like: Helix profit leaves GST out.

Key takeaway
The money you collect is held for the ATO (the tax office), not earned by you, so set it aside.
